lines: Pat the chicken dry and season all over with the salt.
Heat the oil in a wide braiser over medium-high heat. Brown the thighs skin side down until deep golden, about 8 minutes, then turn and cook 2 minutes more. Move to a plate.
Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat. Add the leeks and garlic and cook, stirring, until soft and just starting to colour, 6 to 8 minutes.
Add the wine and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer until nearly gone, about 3 minutes, then stir in the stock, mustard, and thyme.
Return the chicken skin side up, nestling it into the leeks. Braise uncovered in a 375°F oven for 25 minutes.
Stir the crème fraîche into the sauce around the chicken and serve.

lines: Bring the lentils, water, and turmeric to a boil in a large pot. Skim, lower the heat, and simmer until the lentils collapse, 20 to 25 minutes.
Stir in the salt and spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Heat the ghee in a small pan until shimmering. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook until golden, about 6 minutes, then the garlic, ginger, and chile for 1 minute more.
Pour the tadka over the dal and stir it through at the table.

lines: Put a 10-inch cast-iron skillet in the oven and heat to 425°F.
Melt the butter in a small pan and cook, swirling, until it smells nutty and the solids are brown, about 5 minutes.
Whisk the dry ingredients together. Whisk the buttermilk and eggs, then stir them in with all but 1 tablespoon of the butter.
Brush the hot skillet with the last of the butter, pour in the batter, and bake until the top is golden, 20 to 25 minutes.

lines: Heat the oven to 450°F with a sheet pan inside.
Toss the broccoli with the oil and salt, spread it on the hot pan, and roast until charred at the edges, 18 to 20 minutes.
Finish with the zest and juice of the lemon, the chile, and the Parmesan.

lines: Bring the water to a boil, stir in the oats and salt, then turn off the heat, cover, and leave overnight.
In the morning, simmer for 10 minutes, stirring, until creamy. Serve with maple syrup and walnuts.

lines: Season the pork with the salt. Brown it in batches in the oil in a Dutch oven, about 10 minutes per batch.
Lower the heat, add the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic, and cook until soft, 8 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the wine and reduce by half, then the tomatoes, crushing them by hand. Return the pork.
Cover and braise in a 300°F oven until the pork falls apart, 2 1/2 to 3 hours. Shred it into the sauce.
Cook the pappardelle, toss with the ragù and a splash of pasta water, and serve.

lines: Heat the oven to 325°F. Oil a 9-inch springform pan and line the base with parchment.
Whisk the cocoa into the boiling water until smooth, then let it cool slightly.
Beat the sugar, oil, and eggs until pale and thick, about 3 minutes. Fold in the cocoa mixture, almond flour, and baking soda.
Bake until the top is set and a skewer comes out with moist crumbs, 40 to 45 minutes. Cool in the pan.

lines: Melt the butter in a wide pot and cook the shallots until soft, 4 minutes. Crumble in the saffron.
Add the wine, bring to a boil, then add the mussels. Cover and steam, shaking the pot, until they open, 5 to 6 minutes.
Discard any that stay shut. Scatter with parsley and serve with bread for the broth.
